Durchlauchtigſter Fürſt
Gnädigsten Fürst und Herr!
Die Vollmachten und Blanquets sind eingegangen, ich habe von erstem
sogleich den nötigen Gebrauch gemacht, und bin nun des Besten Erfolges
gewis — durch die Vermittelung des braven Generals und des
andern Herrn — wird dH. Gros Kanzler aus den Justiz Fond 90000 rt.
geben — davon bezahle ich die 3 Unruhigsten Gläubiger — das ist
Weigel, die Schlabrendorff und Lichnowski.
Lezterer muß mich auf eine Schweinersche Hypotheque die
ich ihm verpfände 20000 rt zurückgeben, 10000 rt muß ich so
suchen heraus zu bringen, und dan erhalten Ewr Durchlaucht den
gewünschten 30000 rt.
Schlimm ist es daß der Hypothequen Schein der Zagorower und
Trąbczyner Güter so bunt ist, man will darauf nicht weiter
borgen — was man giebt, ist gegen Jura Ca[u?]sa. Es wird sich
indes nach und nach alles machen laßen.
Mein einziges Bestreben ist den Oppenheimer, der voriges Jahr
160000 rt zu geben versprach, und den Amelang bearbeitete
nur bald los zu werden, damit ich die Hypotheque von 250000 rt zu¬
rük bekomme.
Der Schuft hatte selbst zu fordern auf Olesnica. 20000 rt.
er machte sich an heischig die Invaliden Casse zu bezahlen 50000 rtl
dem Lichnowski 36000 rt.
dem Meyer Bernhard 7600.
Sind 113600 rt.
Von diesen allen hatt er nur 32000 rt an Lichnowchen bezahlt
dazu das Geld was Ewr Durchlaucht nach Fürth erhielten
und demohngeachtet rechnet sich der Kerl das ganze
Proxeneticum mit 11000 rt.
Bin ich nun mit Weigel um den andern auseinander
den wende ich alles an um diesen Gau[?]rr das zu bezahlen
was er würklich gegeben hatt, und schaffe sofort die
oben genannte Hypotheque zu rücken die das eo ipso
vernichtet wird, wodurch die Sache alsdan eine ganz
andere Gestallt gewinnt.
Heute gehe ich nach Betsche u. dorten alles zu ordnen, besonders
dem elenden Juden den Meyer Bernhard das Maul zu stopfen
Der Kerl hat gegen Ewr Durchlaucht Klage erhoben, ohnerachtet
ich den Wicht bekannt gemacht hatte daß Sr Majestät die Betscher
Verabpachtung genehmiget und alle Schwierigkeiten dergestalt behoben hätte.
daß Ewr Durch ex nexu gesezt wären.
von Betsche gehe ich nach Kalisz und Trąbczyn arrangere dorten
alles sehe was ich daselbst an Geld zusammen treiben kan und eile
damit hierher um da die Haupt Sache zu Applaniren. Von heut
über 18 Tage gedenke ich wieder in Berlin zu sein und geht nun
alles nach Wunsch so bringe ich dan vieleicht selbst die von Ewr Durchlaucht
laucht gewünschte Summa nach Öhringen.
die Constellationen sind übrigens jezt sehr böse und man wünscht
hier sehr daß Ewr Durchlaucht nur recht baldgöllig hergestellt sei,
mögten, und daß Sie Ihre Rückreise über Berlin nehmen
Durch meinen langen Aufenthalt hier wäre ich lezthin beinahe
in einer günstigen Situation versezt worden. Die Glogausche
Regierung hatte befohlen der v Wulffen 30000 rt welche auf
Kontop stehen zu bezahlen. Die Mandate waren in Breslau liegen
geblieben, so daß ich nichts davon wüste, bis man mir hier auf den
Hals gieng. Indes half hier gleich der bidere General Er gab mir
baar was ich brauchte, und dHerr Gros Kanzler lies auf der einen
Hypotheque 200000 rt zahlen, und so statteten mich diese beide
redlichen Männer — Jezt habe ich ganz ruhe und kan nun alle
Ewr Durchlaucht Sachen nachgehen.
Mit unbegränzter Verehrung verharre ich als
Ewr Durchlaucht
Berlin den 17ten Juny
1806.
treu unterthäniger Diener
v Triebenfeld

Bin ich nun mit Weigel um den andern auseinander den wende ich alles an um diesen Gau[?]rr das zu bezahlen was er würklich gegeben hatt, und schaffe sofort die oben genannte Hypotheque zu rücken die das eo ipso vernichtet wird, wodurch die Sache alsdan eine ganz andere Gestallt gewinnt.

Von heut über 18 Tage gedenke ich wieder in Berlin zu sein und geht nun alles nach Wunsch so bringe ich dan vieleicht selbst die von Ewr Durchlaucht laucht gewünschte Summa nach Öhringen.

translation.en:
187

Most Serene Prince

Most gracious Prince and Lord!

The powers of attorney and the blank forms have arrived; of the first I at once made the necessary use, and I am now assured of the best success — through the mediation of the worthy General and of the other gentleman — the Lord Grand Chancellor will give 90000 Rthl out of the Justice Fund — out of which I shall pay the 3 most restive creditors — that is, Weigel, the Schlabrendorff lady and Lichnowski.

The last named must return to me 20000 Rthl against a Świniary mortgage which I pledge to him; 10000 Rthl I must contrive to raise in like manner, and then Your Serene Highness will receive the desired 30000 Rthl.

It is a bad thing that the mortgage certificate of the Zagórów and Trąbczyn estates is so motley; nobody will lend any further upon it — what is given is against Jura Ca[uncertain: u]sa. In time, however, it will all be manageable.

My single endeavour is to be rid, and soon, of Oppenheimer, who last year promised to give 160000 Rthl and who worked upon Amelang

only, so that I may get back the mortgage of 250000 Rthl.

The scoundrel himself had a claim upon Oleśnica of 20000 Rthl; he undertook to pay the Invalids' Fund 50000 Rthl, to Lichnowski 36000 Rthl.

to Meyer Bernhard 7600.

That is 113600 Rthl.

Of all these he has paid only 32000 Rthl to Lichnowchen, together with the money which Your Serene Highness received at Fürth, and notwithstanding this the fellow reckons the whole brokerage to himself at 11000 Rthl.

Once I am clear of Weigel and the other, I shall apply everything to making this [illegible] pay what he has really given, and shall at once procure the above-named mortgage back, which is thereby annulled eo ipso, whereby the matter then takes on quite another shape.

Today I go to Pszczew, and there to set everything in order, in particular to stop the mouth of that wretched Jew Meyer Bernhard. The fellow has brought suit against Your Serene Highness, notwithstanding that I had made it known to the knave that His Majesty had approved the Pszczew

lease and had removed all difficulties in such a manner that Your Serene Highness was released from the obligation (ex nexu).

From Pszczew I go to Kalisz and Trąbczyn, arrange everything there, see what money I can gather in at that place, and hasten back here with it in order to smooth out the principal business. Eighteen days from today I expect to be in Berlin again, and if all now goes as wished, I shall then perhaps myself bring to Öhringen the sum desired by Your Serene Highness.

The constellations, moreover, are now very evil, and it is much wished here that Your Serene Highness might be quite soon entirely restored to health, and that you would take your return journey by way of Berlin. Through my long stay here I was lately very nearly placed in a favourable situation. The Głogów Government had ordered that the 30000 Rthl of the von Wulffen lady which stand upon Konotop be paid. The mandates had been left lying in Wrocław, so that I knew nothing of it until they fell upon my neck here. In the meantime the upright General at once helped here; he gave me in cash what I needed, and the Lord Grand Chancellor had 200000 Rthl paid upon the one mortgage, and so these two honest men provided me — Now I have full quiet and can attend to all Your Serene Highness's affairs.

With unbounded reverence I remain, as Your Serene Highness's

text_english:
187

Most Serene Prince

Most gracious Prince and Lord!

The powers of attorney and the blank forms have arrived; of the first I at once made the necessary use, and I am now assured of the best success — through the mediation of the worthy General and of the other gentleman — the Lord Grand Chancellor will give 90000 Rthl out of the Justice Fund — out of which I shall pay the 3 most restive creditors — that is, Weigel, the Schlabrendorff lady and Lichnowski.

The last named must return to me 20000 Rthl against a Świniary mortgage which I pledge to him; 10000 Rthl I must contrive to raise in like manner, and then Your Serene Highness will receive the desired 30000 Rthl.

It is a bad thing that the mortgage certificate of the Zagórów and Trąbczyn estates is so motley; nobody will lend any further upon it — what is given is against Jura Ca[uncertain: u]sa. In time, however, it will all be manageable.

My single endeavour is to be rid, and soon, of Oppenheimer, who last year promised to give 160000 Rthl and who worked upon Amelang

only, so that I may get back the mortgage of 250000 Rthl.

The scoundrel himself had a claim upon Oleśnica of 20000 Rthl; he undertook to pay the Invalids' Fund 50000 Rthl, to Lichnowski 36000 Rthl.

to Meyer Bernhard 7600.

That is 113600 Rthl.

Of all these he has paid only 32000 Rthl to Lichnowchen, together with the money which Your Serene Highness received at Fürth, and notwithstanding this the fellow reckons the whole brokerage to himself at 11000 Rthl.

Once I am clear of Weigel and the other, I shall apply everything to making this [illegible] pay what he has really given, and shall at once procure the above-named mortgage back, which is thereby annulled eo ipso, whereby the matter then takes on quite another shape.

Today I go to Pszczew, and there to set everything in order, in particular to stop the mouth of that wretched Jew Meyer Bernhard. The fellow has brought suit against Your Serene Highness, notwithstanding that I had made it known to the knave that His Majesty had approved the Pszczew

lease and had removed all difficulties in such a manner that Your Serene Highness was released from the obligation (ex nexu).

From Pszczew I go to Kalisz and Trąbczyn, arrange everything there, see what money I can gather in at that place, and hasten back here with it in order to smooth out the principal business. Eighteen days from today I expect to be in Berlin again, and if all now goes as wished, I shall then perhaps myself bring to Öhringen the sum desired by Your Serene Highness.

The constellations, moreover, are now very evil, and it is much wished here that Your Serene Highness might be quite soon entirely restored to health, and that you would take your return journey by way of Berlin. Through my long stay here I was lately very nearly placed in a favourable situation. The Głogów Government had ordered that the 30000 Rthl of the von Wulffen lady which stand upon Konotop be paid. The mandates had been left lying in Wrocław, so that I knew nothing of it until they fell upon my neck here. In the meantime the upright General at once helped here; he gave me in cash what I needed, and the Lord Grand Chancellor had 200000 Rthl paid upon the one mortgage, and so these two honest men provided me — Now I have full quiet and can attend to all Your Serene Highness's affairs.

With unbounded reverence I remain, as Your Serene Highness's

Berlin, the 17th of June

1806.

faithful, humble and obedient servant

v Triebenfeld

reading.notes: Triebenfeld in Berlin writes to the Prince. The powers of attorney he had asked for (doc. 185) have arrived. With the help of the General, the Gros Kanzler will provide 90000 rt from the Justiz Fond to pay Weigel, Schlabrendorff and Lichnowski. Lichnowski is to return 20000 rt against a mortgage on Świniary, and then the Prince gets his 30000 rt. The mortgage register of Zagórów and Trąbczyn is so encumbered that nobody will lend more. He wants to be rid of Oppenheimer so he can recover the 250000 rt mortgage, and he lists Oppenheimer's unmet obligations. He plans trips to Betsche (Meyer Bernhard's lawsuit), Kalisz and Trąbczyn. He also describes the Wulffen/Kontop payment demand.
